value.body:
Two decisions from Jack Heart, 2026-11-14. (1) Failure: "is this just adding a reason onto failed, a failed retry = true, something like that?" Yes. Replaces conclusion F's separate outcome: a match has one failed status carrying `retry: bool`. Prior art: Dagster RetryRequested, Temporal non-retryable errors, Kubernetes podFailurePolicy. Etude's own infrastructure failures (server process exited, deadline, delivery) are failed with retry=true; an exception from play is failed with retry=false unless play raises Etude's one retry exception. A retry=true match stays eligible for the next pass and never counts as a result; any failed match fails the run, so a refused pass is never recorded succeeded. Rows that merely say a game was invalid are the author's to turn into a raise; document it. (2) Game processes: "fine to say that the inference server hosts game processes too ... The eval job is really just a light sort of match definition ... Maybe it should even be that more transparent". So with a server, Etude starts no worker pool for the group: it enters the server once and hands each match to it; the server plays the match in its own game processes and owns how many are active. Without a server, today's worker pool calls play(match). Make that visible in the API rather than hiding a relay: an EvalJob says what to play (tournament, checkpoints, and either play or server), and the docs say which process plays. Since the server now plays games, check whether InferenceServer is still the right name and propose one in the PR description rather than renaming silently.
